name: AUSTRIA

flag.title: Flag of Austria
flag.note: One of the oldest flags in Europe

lead: Austria is a small, landlocked country in the heart of Europe, ringed by the towering Alps. Once the centre of a grand empire ruling much of Europe, today it is famous for soaring mountain scenery, grand concert halls, and pastries so good that the whole world borrowed its recipes — from croissants to apple strudel.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go WOW

geo: Austria is almost entirely covered by the Alps, with snow-capped peaks, deep green valleys, and glacial lakes. The Danube River — made famous by a waltz — flows through the northern lowlands and past Vienna.
To the east the land flattens into the Vienna Basin, where most Austrians live and farm. Austria shares borders with eight countries, more neighbours than almost any nation its size.
animals: The high Alps are home to the chamois, a sure-footed mountain antelope that leaps between rocky ledges, and the ibex with its enormous curved horns. Golden eagles soar overhead on the mountain thermals.

In the forests below, red deer, brown bears, and lynx roam quietly. The white Lipizzan horses — famous for their breathtaking dancing displays — were bred in Austria and remain a proud national symbol.
culture: Austria gave the world some of its greatest composers — Mozart was born in Salzburg, and the Strauss family invented the waltz. Vienna's concert halls still sell out every night with music lovers.
Austrians take coffee very seriously. The Viennese coffeehouse — a cosy café where people linger over a Melange and a slice of Sachertorte — is UNESCO intangible cultural heritage.
history: Austria was the heartland of the Habsburg dynasty, which ruled a vast empire across Central Europe for over 600 years. At its peak the empire stretched from Spain to Hungary, making Vienna one of the world's most powerful cities.

After World War I the empire collapsed and Austria became a republic. Absorbed by Nazi Germany in 1938, then liberated in 1945, Austria declared permanent neutrality in 1955 — a promise it still keeps today.
wows: Mozart wrote his first symphony aged eight — in London, not Salzburg, while on a European family tour.
Austria invented the croissant — Vienna's bakers created it, and France later made it world-famous.
Vienna's New Year's Concert is broadcast to over 150 countries every 1 January.
Großglockner High Alpine Road rises so steeply that drivers pass through four distinct climate zones.
Austria is one of the top nations on Earth for Winter Olympic medals per person.
Vienna's Spanish Riding School has trained Lipizzan horses the same way for over 450 years.
Red Bull was invented in Austria in 1987 after its founder tried a similar drink in Thailand.

myths.myth: "Austria and Australia are the same place"
myths.fact: Austria is a small landlocked country in Central Europe; Australia is a continent-island on the other side of the planet, about 140 times bigger and surrounded by ocean.
Mozart was born in 1756 in Salzburg, which is very much in Austria — and Austrians are extremely proud of him.
